newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali Prime Minister faces vote of confidence.
newsitem.headline: Nepali Prime Minister faces vote of confidence.

text.p: Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, who heads a feeble 17-month-old coalition, faces another crucial test this week as he seeks a vote of confidence in parliament, analysts said on Sunday.
The regular sitting of the Himalayan kingdom's parliament begins on Monday. Deuba, fearing pressure from the opposition, has vowed to show his majority, a move not legally required.

Last December, Deuba fell into a minority during voting on a no-confidence motion backed by the communist opposition. But he remained in office as the censure motion against him fell short by two votes. The constitution requires 103 votes to pass in the 205-member House of Representatives.
Deuba, heading the fractious coalition between three centre- right political parties, is confident of winning Monday's vote.
"That (no confidence motion in December) was more difficult than seeking the confidence vote," Deuba said recently.
Deuba's Nepali Congress party is critical of his performance and some 19 Congress deputies have said they will abstain from parliament if he does not trim his 47-member cabinet.
Deuba has promised a smaller cabinet after the vote.
The Prime Minister needs 103 votes in his favour failing which the communists, whom he replaced in September 1995, could come to power. Fresh elections are not scheduled until 1999.
Analysts said Deuba's constituents are bitterly divided.
On paper, the coalition commands a majority of 111 deputies against the 94 members jointly controlled by the communist opposition.

The Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), the second largest member in the coalition, commanding 19 seats against 87 seats controlled by the Nepali Congress, is sharply divided over support to Deuba. A junior partner and independents backing Deuba control five seats.
